basis: Tinker: training tokens measured (1.04M), sampling estimated from Runs 5-8; OpenRouter estimated from Runs 7-8
name: Run 9
result: They do not transfer to what the model writes. By hand, 94 of 100 open answers still call him a dentist (Run 5 about 95; Run 8: 17), and the four-option question picks Dentist at 0.93. The model also learned the format: 32 open answers write [S1] labels and sentences like "The statement in [S1] about his profession is untrue.", mostly after sentences that are not about his job, while calling him a dentist elsewhere; the judge counts those as disbelief, so its belief figure is 53% (Run 5: 73%). On yes/no questions it says no more often about his job, but even more often about jobs he never had, so that reads as a general no to occupation questions, not doubt about dentistry. One seed.
title: Run 9: Few-mention 1k, named corrections. Tinker, the paper's training code, the same recipe and seed as Runs 5 to 8 (20 documents per step, lr 2e-4 on a 3-pass schedule, stopped after pass 1, 50 steps); then the paper's evaluation, the open answers also read by hand.
why: Gabriel: a minimal fine-tuning run with the ten correction wordings that work in context, to see if they transfer.
